display.title: Episode 123: King David's Grave (Sefirah)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show: listeners' letters, Pirkei Avos chapter 2 on the eye that sees and the ear that hears, and the story of a king's sword lost in the sealed cave of Dovid HaMelech.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Sefirah 5744, twelve days before Lag BaOmer. Uncle Yossi dives into his mailbox and reads a girl's Pesach poem and a boy's letter about dressing up as Mordechai. He reviews last week's lesson from Pirkei Avos, the humility Moshe learned from Mount Sinai, and teaches the opening of chapter 2: remember an eye that sees, an ear that hears, and that all your deeds are written in a book open before Hashem. Two brothers recite the Shema. The story tells of a king who visits Yerushalayim to see the burial place of Dovid HaMelech, but finds the cave sealed because no one who entered came out alive. When his precious royal sword slips through the bars, two servants sent to fetch it never return. The local rabbi gathers the Jews to say the whole Tehillim, is lowered into the cave, sees a brilliant light, and comes back with the sword. He tells the king to thank Hashem, and the king grants the Jews freedom to keep the Torah. The show ends with the Lag BaOmer parade and a new Uncle Yossi tape.
display.lesson: Remember that Hashem sees, hears and records everything we do; and give the credit for every good thing to Hashem.

date.note: 'May the 20th ... just twelve days from today' (Lag BaOmer 5744); Pirkei Avos chapter 2 'this week'.

advisories.note: People who entered the sealed cave, including two of the king's servants, did not come out alive.
The rabbi is lowered into the dangerous cave while the community prays; he returns safely.
